review_notes: I read the whole target file, plus the definitions of information, rowMass and conditionalMass in Logarithms.lean and FiniteTables.lean. I also grepped the Information directory for other uses of conditionalMass and rowMass. The file has no simp attributes, and `jointMass_eq_row_mul_conditional` should not be made simp: its right-hand side contains the left-hand side `q v y` inside `conditionalMass`, so it risks looping and it has a hypothesis. The findings are about missing canonical simp lemmas, which show up as repeated ad hoc unfolding. I did not run Lean, so I make no claims about how the simplifier actually behaves. The real uncertainty is how many call sites would shrink after the change.

findings.problem: `conditionalMass` has no simp-facing API. The degenerate case (row mass zero, so the conditional mass is `q v y / 0 = 0`) is handled by unfolding the definition in each proof. This file does it at line 102 and again at lines 89–93 (`simp [hv, hq0]` and `unfold conditionalMass; field_simp`). FiniteTables.lean does it at line 223 (`unfold conditionalMass` followed by `simp only [hr, div_zero, zero_le_one]`). Entropy.lean and EntropyLaws.lean also use `unfold ... conditionalMass`. Unfolding exposes `q v y / ∑ y, q v y`, so the canonical `conditionalMass` form is lost.
findings.proposed_change: In FiniteTables.lean, next to the definition, add `@[simp] lemma conditionalMass_of_rowMass_eq_zero (q) (v) (y) (h : rowMass q v = 0) : conditionalMass q v y = 0 := by simp [conditionalMass, h]`. Add `conditionalMass_def` as an unfolding lemma (`conditionalMass q v y = q v y / rowMass q v`, proved by `rfl`) and use it for the non-degenerate case. The side condition `rowMass q v = 0` can be discharged by simp when `hr` is in the simp set, so the call sites become `simp [hr]`. Keep `conditionalMass` itself irreducible-by-simp, with no `@[simp]` unfolding.
findings.benefit: The zero-row case is stated once. The bounds proofs (`conditional_information_nonneg`, `conditionalEntropy_nonneg`) stay in terms of `conditionalMass`, and the duplicated `unfold conditionalMass` plus case-split blocks shrink.

rw [← Finset.sum_mul]
      simp only [rowMass, hq1, one_mul]
findings.problem: The proofs finish by unfolding `rowMass` inside `simp only`, so that `∑ v, rowMass q v` turns into the double sum that `hq1` rewrites. There is no lemma saying the total row mass is 1. The same unfold-then-rewrite step appears in the second lemma (lines 163–165) and in FiniteTables.lean line 83 (`simp only [rowMass, hq1, mul_one]`). FiniteTables.lean line 161 works around it with `have hrow : ∑ v, rowMass q v = 1 := hq1`. `Conditioning.lean` defines `totalMass` as `∑ v, rowMass q v`, so the gap is real.
findings.proposed_change: In FiniteTables.lean, add `lemma sum_rowMass_eq_one (q : V → Y → ℝ) (hq1 : ∑ v, ∑ y, q v y = 1) : ∑ v, rowMass q v = 1 := hq1`. Optionally add the unconditional `sum_rowMass : ∑ v, rowMass q v = ∑ v, ∑ y, q v y := rfl` and tag it `@[simp]`; this is a safe orientation because it only unfolds a definition into its canonical double-sum form. Then the endings become `rw [← Finset.sum_mul, sum_rowMass_eq_one q hq1, one_mul]`, or `simp [sum_rowMass_eq_one q hq1]`.
findings.benefit: The proofs stop depending on how `rowMass` is defined. The three call sites and the `hrow` workaround share one named fact, and a change to the `rowMass` definition would not break them.
